title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, and Top Support Issues
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates the canonical patterns, quickstarts, SDK guidance, API examples, and the top support issues + canonical fixes the Developer Experience (DevEx) team publishes for Redwood Inference customers and internal engineers. It is a reference intended for SDK authors, docs writers, solutions engineers, and on-call support.

Scope: SDK (Python, Node), quickstart templates (app + backend), canonical API examples (text generation, chat, embeddings, streaming, function/tool calling), docs-site operating procedures (publishing, review, rollbacks), and the top support issues with step-by-step canonical fixes.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new and returning users (target 10-minute quickstart completion).
- Reduce recurring support volume by publishing canonical fixes and playbooks.
- Ensure SDKs and examples reflect current API semantics and recommended best practices.

Owners and contacts
- Document owner: Developer Experience (DevEx) docs subteam. Primary contact: Priya Nair (priya@redwood.example).
- SDK owners: SDK Platform (owner: Evan Chen).
- On-call support contact for docs regressions: docs-oncall@redwood.example.

Conventions and publishing rules
- All examples MUST use the latest stable API version (see API version in header of examples).
- Use short, copy-paste-ready snippets (<=25 lines) for quickstarts; link to full example repos for longer samples.
- Tests: every code example included in the docs site must have an associated CI smoke test (see Docs CI section below).
- Use the standardized disclaimer and SLOs block at the top of all quickstarts.

Quickstarts and templates (recommended structure)
- Each quickstart repo should follow the same layout: 
  - /README.md (overview, prerequisites, run steps)
  - /examples/ (copy-paste snippets used in the guide)
  - /src/ (app code)
  - /ci/ (smoke tests that run against local emulator or staging)
  - /LICENSE, /CODE_OF_CONDUCT

Example quickstart objective: "Build a minimal customer support summarization service using Redwood API (Python)"
- Expected completion time: 10 minutes (local) or 20 minutes (cloud).
- Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip, Redwood API key (free dev credits).

Python SDK quickstart (minimal flow)
1) Install
   ```bash
   pip install redwood-inference-sdk
   ```
2) Minimal snippet (text generation)
   ```python
   from redwood import RedwoodClient

   client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
   resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-alpha-1", prompt="Summarize: Our user reported a payment failure.")
   print(resp.text)
   ```
3) Helpful tips: use streaming for UX-sensitive flows; use prefix caching for repeated prompts.

Node SDK quickstart (minimal flow)
1) Install
   ```bash
   npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
   ```
2) Minimal snippet (embeddings + search)
   ```js
   import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
   const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
   const emb = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'redwood-embed-1', input: 'How do I reset my password?' });
   console.log(emb.data[0].embedding.length);
   ```

API examples (canonical patterns)
- Text generation (sync): show minimal request, error handling, retry policy.
- Streaming text (server-sent-events / WebSocket): show client and server usage, heartbeat, reconnect.
- Chat with function calling: show structured tool outputs, explicit schema examples.
- Embeddings + vector search: provide heuristic for chunk size, embedding dimensionality, and index refresh cadence.

Canonical API example: text generation (curl)
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Translate to French: Hello, world!","max_tokens":60}'
```

Docs site operating procedures (publishing workflow)
1) Authoring: create a feature branch and draft the page in the docs repo. Use the docs template: docs/templates/quickstart-template.md.
2) Smoke tests: add a smoke test that runs the core example; link test in the PR description (CI job: docs-smoke).
3) Review: request 2 reviewers: one SDK owner + one DevEx writer. Use PR label: docs-ready-for-review.
4) Merge: devex lead must approve for major changes. Small fixes can be approved by one reviewer.
5) Release: the docs site build (Netlify) picks up main branch and deploys. Expect propagation within 5 minutes for CDN.
6) Rollback: if a regression is detected, revert the PR and follow the Incident Playbook (link below).

Change log and versioning
- All quickstarts should include a small changelog header with date and author.
- Major SDK examples must include the SDK version used in the snippet: e.g., `redwood-inference-sdk==0.9.2`

Docs CI and smoke tests
- CI job 'docs-smoke' runs code examples in a sandbox environment using ephemeral API keys.
- Failure thresholds: if >3 smoke tests fail in a run, block the PR and notify docs-oncall.
- Test matrix includes: Python 3.10, Node 18, and our internal docs emulator (emulates basic API responses).

Top support issues and canonical fixes (canonicalized Q&A for first-tier support)
1) "API returns 401 Unauthorized"
   - Symptom: Errors like {"error":{"code":401,"message":"invalid API key"}}
   - Cause: Missing/rotated key or environment var not set in CI.
   - Detection: Reproduce with `curl` using same key; check request headers in logs.
   - Fast fix: Ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set; rotate key if compromised.
   - Permanent fix: Store keys in vault/KMS and use short-lived tokens for CI.

2) "High p95 latency on generation (sudden spike)"
   - Symptom: p95 > 1s for generation endpoints (normally p95 < 300ms).
   - Cause: Model autoscaler lag, large batch build-up, or cross-region routing to high-latency region.
   - Detection: Check routing logs, batch queue length, and model instance health in observability dashboard.
   - Fast fix: Promote reserved capacity (if on Dedicated) or re-route traffic to a lower-latency region. Restart lagging instances if needed.
   - Permanent fix: Adjust autoscaler policies, introduce backpressure at gateway, and add a surge buffer of warm instances.

3) "Incorrect outputs after SDK upgrade"
   - Symptom: API responses change shape or keys differ after SDK bump.
   - Cause: Breaking change in SDK serialization or API version mismatch.
   - Detection: Run unit tests that exercise the SDK example code; compare HTTP request/response shapes.
   - Fast fix: Pin SDK to previous working version in the quickstart and open a compatibility PR.
   - Permanent fix: Add integration tests into SDK release pipeline and coordinate coordinated release notes.

4) "Streaming disconnects mid-response"
   - Symptom: Client stops receiving data before message end; connection resets.
   - Cause: Unstable network, incorrect SSE heartbeat, or client read timeout.
   - Detection: Reproduce with a controlled client; check gateway logs for dropped connections.
   - Fast fix: Increase client read timeout and implement reconnect logic with resume tokens.
   - Permanent fix: Harden proxy timeout defaults and add server-side keepalive for streaming sessions.

5) "Embeddings dimensionality mismatch in downstream index"
   - Symptom: Index rejects embedding vectors or distances are incorrect.
   - Cause: Using embeddings from different model or wrong serialization (float32 vs float16).
   - Detection: Validate vector length and type when ingesting.
   - Fast fix: Recompute embeddings with the correct model and re-index.
   - Permanent fix: Add an ingestion validator that checks dimension and model meta before accepting vectors.

6) "Function calling returns invalid JSON / schema mismatch"
   - Symptom: Tools receive malformed JSON or unexpected fields.
   - Cause: Model produced non-JSON tokens or schema not enforced in the request.
   - Detection: Compare tool payload vs schema in logs; run the eval harness.
   - Fast fix: Strictly validate and reject non-JSON payloads at the gateway.
   - Permanent fix: Use structured output modes with enforced schemas and fallback parsing rules.

7) "Excessive token usage for many small prompts"
   - Symptom: Unexpectedly high token consumption for chat endpoints.
   - Cause: Not using prefix caching or redundant system messages across calls.
   - Detection: Check token-per-call metrics in the usage dashboard.
   - Fast fix: Consolidate prompts, remove repetitive content, enable prefix/KV caching.
   - Permanent fix: Educate customers via quickstart patterns and implement server-side caching heuristics.

8) "Docs examples out-of-date after API change"
   - Symptom: Examples fail or CI smoke tests break after API rollout.
   - Cause: Missing coordination between API and docs teams.
   - Detection: CI smoke test failures and automated docs link checker alerts.
   - Fast fix: Revert docs to last passing commit and open a targeted docs PR to update examples.
   - Permanent fix: Add a docs gating policy: API changes that alter public request/response shapes must publish a docs compatibility matrix at least 48 hours before rollout.

Canonical fix checklist (for support engineers)
1) Reproduce the issue locally or in the staging sandbox.
2) Capture request/response and relevant logs; redact PII and keys.
3) Apply the documented fast fix and confirm customer success.
4) Open a follow-up ticket for permanent fix and link to this doc.

Appendix: useful CLI commands and example configs
- Check API key (curl)
  ```bash
  curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
  ```
- Example docs smoke test (bash)
  ```bash
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY="${TEST_API_KEY}"
  python examples/smoke_test_python_quickstart.py
  ```
- Example service YAML for quickstart (text generation worker)
  | field | example | notes |
  |---|---|---|
  | replicas | 2 | scale to 4 for production |
  | model | redwood-alpha-1 | pin to a stable variant for reproducibility |
  | timeout_ms | 800 | request timeout before fallback |
